subject: Skyline / skyline-7b: compatibility check + temporary pin request
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@skyline.ai>, partners@skyline.ai
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Skyline / skyline-7b: compatibility check + temporary pin request

Hi Jordan (and Skyline team),

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising for our Dedicated SKU. Before we start a larger ingestion, we need two quick items from your side so we can greenlight an onboard in staging:

1) A short compatibility checklist (model card + any non-standard ops) we can run through our kernel selector and quantization tests.
2) Your recommended config for KV caching and any warnings around long context streaming (we saw some potential tokenization differences in the demo).

Separately, our infra/product teams are asking for a temporary "pin" on the skyline-7b variant while we complete compatibility tests so that customer traffic doesn't get routed to a newly published skyline-7b-2.0 that might break KV cache assumptions. Is Skyline comfortable with an explicit compatible-variant tag we can reference?

I've attached the model card you shared and a first-draft test plan we want to run. Dev/Monica — FYI on product ask and timeline (we'd like a staging verdict by EOD May 11).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Product Manager, Model Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: skyline_model_card.pdf, compat-test-plan.md
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@skyline.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Skyline / skyline-7b: compatibility check + temporary pin request

Kim / Jordan —

Quick technical readout from my side after the first pass: we ran the model through our tokenization and quantization smoke tests. High-level notes:

- Tokenization: baseline mapping looks consistent, but there are ~0.3% tokens that get split differently when we switch to byte-level BPE in our streaming path. This affects prefix cache hits for long-context prompt reuse.
- Ops: skyline-7b references a fused-attention kernel variant that isn't in our optimized kernel set yet. We'll need a fallback path (slower) or a small kernel backport on the serving side.
- KV caching: the model's default attention window supports key/value sizes up to 16k tokens; caching semantics look fine but we need to validate hot-reload of cache entries during model swap.

Action items for us:
1) Run the full compat-test-plan.md in staging (estimated 18 hours wall-time with current infra).
2) If Skyline can publish a pinned compatible tag (e.g., skyline-7b@v1.0-compatible) we can set routing rules to prefer the tag until we finish tests.
3) If the fused kernel is required for perf, we can either backport the kernel (security review required) or run the model on a slower fallback path for the first 72 hours.

Jordan — can you confirm whether Skyline can publish a stable-compatible tag and whether the fused kernel is mandatory for the benchmark numbers you shared?

- Dev
Principal Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Skyline / skyline-7b: compatibility check + temporary pin request

Hi Dev / Kim / team,

Thanks for the thorough pass — appreciate the specifics. Short answers:

- We can publish a compatible tag. We'll push skyline-7b@redwood-compatible-v1 on Monday and leave it immutable for at least two weeks while you run tests.
- The fused-attention kernel is recommended for the perf numbers we quoted but is not strictly required; performance will drop ~12-18% on the CPU fallback and ~6-9% on our generic GPU kernel.
- We'll add a short note in the model card about tokenization edge-cases and provide a small script that normalizes inputs to your streaming BPE.

We'll attach the updated model card and the normalization script to the Drive link; you should see it in the related links I shared. Let me know if you need signed NDA addendums for kernel code.

Jordan
Partner Engineering, Skyline AI

Folks — quick operational decision:

- Per product roadmap and SLA exposure for the early access customer cohort, we should accept Jordan's compatible tag and proceed with the full staging run today.
- Lauren — can you approve a one-week exception to the model-variant auto-update policy so that routing won't auto-promote skyline-7b-2.0 into the Dedicated pool during verification? This is the temporary pin I referenced.
- Dev — run the compat-test-plan.md; if any blocker (fused-kernel or tokenization drift) is flagged as critical, escalate to Lauren and me.

If Lauren approves, I will send a short notice to the CS/ops rotation so they aren't surprised by a pinned variant.

Monica Patel
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
